title: The welcome screen and its piano
description: docs/audio.md § Where music plays now: the release opens on the welcome screen (development with ?title): the game's name and one button, «Nueva partida» for a new game, over Gerard's room at night, blurred. Aitor's piano (intro-piano) plays under it from its first note as soon as sound is on: at once where the browser lets the page play (as the test browser does), otherwise on the first press, which then only brings the piano in; the next press starts the game, in the house, where triste comes over the piano. The scenario suspends sound to play that second case. With a game under way the button says «Continuar». The overlay is the scenario's, not the game's. It plays music, so run it with --chrome: just screenshots title --chrome.

steps.eval: window.showMusic = () => { let el = document.querySelector('#music-check'); if (!el) { el = document.createElement('div'); el.id = 'music-check'; el.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:16px;bottom:16px;z-index:999;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:8px;background:#000c;color:#ffd6ec;font:14px/1.4 monospace'; document.body.append(el); } const m = window.gerard.music; el.textContent = `♪ ${m.playing ?? 'silencio'} · ${m.position()?.toFixed(2) ?? '—'} s · sonido ${window.gerard.audio.running ? 'activo' : 'bloqueado'}`; }

steps.caption: A new game: the name and «Nueva partida», nothing else, with the piano from its first note (this browser lets the page play)
Where the browser keeps sound off until a gesture (played here by suspending it)…
…the first press only turns it on: the piano plays, and the screen still waits
The next press starts the game in the house: triste comes over the piano
